problem: Find the minimum value of $Q(x)=-3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2}$ given that $‖x‖=1.$
worked_solution:
First, notice that ${x}_{1}^{2}\ge 0$ and ${x}_{3}^{2}\ge 0.$ So, we have that

$$
-3{x}_{1}^{2}\ge -4{x}_{1}^{2},\,5{x}_{3}^{2}\ge -4{x}_{3}^{2}.
$$

As a result, 

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & \ge -4{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}-4{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}).\end{aligned}
$$

Now, recall that $‖x‖=1$ is equivalent to ${x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2}=1.$ So, 

$$
\begin{aligned}-4({x}_{1}^{2}+{x}_{2}^{2}+{x}_{3}^{2})=-4(1)=-4.\end{aligned}
$$

and, in turn, $Q(x)\ge -4.$   

So, the value of $Q(x)$ can be no smaller than $-4.$ But before we conclude that $-4$ is the minimum, we need to find a vector such that $Q(x)=-4.$

Notice that when $x={[\begin{aligned}0 & 1 & 0\end{aligned}]}^{T},$ we get

$$
\begin{aligned}Q(x) & =-3{x}_{1}^{2}-4{x}_{2}^{2}+5{x}_{3}^{2} \\  & =-3(0)^{2}-4(1)^{2}+5(0)^{2} \\  & =-4.\end{aligned}
$$

Therefore, given that $‖x‖=1,$ the minimum value of $Q(x)$ is equal to $-4.$
